This reference maps the frozen v1 API surfaces, called the baseline below, to
their current owners in SCGSim 3.0.

The Solid/Thin-Film 3D request extension requires a request-level `modeling`
value of `"solid"` or `"thin_film"` for
every new Q3D and HFSS 3D request. The field has no default, and an absent mode
is never inferred for those families. Previously supported result payloads
remain readable only under their original family/schema reader with their raw
payload and hash preserved. This does not change the shared versioned handoff
compatibility of unchanged families such as Q2D. Q2D and Palace contracts are
otherwise unchanged.

## AEDT release selection

The current AEDT native-request, saved-field analysis, and handoff APIs require
an explicit `aedt_version` with exactly `"2023.2"` or `"2024.2"`; no release
is inferred or selected by default. This request value travels with the handoff and selects the local
transaction runtime. Both choices use PyAEDT 1.3.0 and run a local AEDT Desktop
on the same host as SCGSim.

AEDT 2023.2 uses PyAEDT's same-node gRPC compatibility settings, scoped to the
transaction and restored through cleanup: `use_grpc_api=True`,
`grpc_secure_mode=False`, `grpc_local=True`, `grpc_listen_all=False`, and
`PYAEDT_USE_PRE_GRPC_ARGS="True"`. AEDT 2024.2 uses no transport overrides.
There is no fallback or downgrade between the requested releases. A saved
artifact's source-version origin is separate from the request and actual
connected version. An unknown origin remains `None`; analysis can still run
using its separately explicit requested release, without lookup or migration.

Package-level facades remain the supported high-level entrypoints. The move
does not add compatibility wrappers for old internal paths. Existing consumer
pins remain unchanged; a consumer migrates only when it deliberately adopts
the current package and the corresponding old-to-new map.

## Migration rules

- Keep `scgsim.geometry`, `scgsim.palace`, `scgsim.aedt`, and
  `scgsim.visualization` as package entrypoints. Palace builds its geometry with
  SGB: see [Palace meshing and Surface EPR](#palace-mesh-migration).
- Treat documented facades and declared exports as public. A private or
  importable implementation module is not automatically a supported API.
- Move each supported symbol to its single responsibility owner and re-export
  the approved high-level symbols from the package facade. Do not leave a
  second old implementation or compatibility wrapper reachable.
- Do not revive Q3D input-v1 or input-v2. Input-v3 on the SGB model is the
  Q3D contract.
- Preserve the formal `python -m scgsim.aedt.run` command as the AEDT
  transaction entrypoint. It is a supported CLI, not a legacy wrapper.
- AEDT receipts record a generated runtime source,
  `scgsim.aedt.runtime-source.v30`: the import closure of the AEDT modules,
  with the SHA-256 of each file. A result recorded under an earlier
  runtime-source schema is refused; read it with the SCGSim commit that wrote
  it. Migration does not rewrite or reinterpret old receipts.

## AEDT studies on the SGB model {#aedt-sgb-migration}

From `3.0.0rc3` an AEDT study prepares every 3D family from a `GeometryPlan` snapshot:
AEDT imports the plan's SGB model, the model Palace meshes, and builds no
geometry of its own (issue #67). A study written for the earlier route meets
four changes.

- **The entry is the plan.** HFSS Eigenmode is `EigenmodeSim.set_plan(snapshot)`
  and `sim.prepare_handoff()`; Driven Terminal is
  `prepare_sgb_model(snapshot.geometry_input, prepared_stack=snapshot.stack,
  ports=...)` and `prepare_hfss_driven_from_geometry(model=...)`; Q3D is
  `prepare_q3d_from_geometry(snapshot, ...)`. The GDS route
  (`HfssEigenmodeSpec`, `HfssDrivenSpec`, `LayerImport`, `ObjectBinding`,
  `LengthMeshSpec`, `gds_path`) and `PreparedPlanarGeometry` are removed;
  the [AEDT API list](#aedt-api-transaction-and-state-ownership) names each
  replacement.
- **The Region is the plan's.** `set_vacuum_region(...)` sets it for every
  family; `region_padding_um` is removed.
- **Driven Modal and wave ports wait for issue #135.** `prepare_sgb_model`
  refuses a `ModalPort` and a wave `TerminalPort`, naming
  [issue #135](https://github.com/NCUPHY-LTLab/scgsim/issues/135). A two-port
  network today is Driven Terminal with `LumpedTerminalPort`s on the plan's
  port sheets.
- **Run folders of the native builder are not read.** `execute_handoff`,
  `resolve_results()` and `analyze_epr()` refuse their handoffs, requests and
  saved solutions. Prepare and run the study again with this version; read an
  old result with the SCGSim commit that wrote it.

## Solid/Thin-Film request migration

New Q3D and HFSS 3D requests require the explicit request-level selection
`modeling="solid"` or `modeling="thin_film"`. Omitting it or supplying another
mode does not select an implicit compatibility path. The PDK/source contract
also supplies exact physical-layer identity, feature kind (stack film, local
film or finite volume), physical thickness, and the film attachment face where
applicable. Existing Object, Net, port, connected
outline and hole identities remain the request's source of truth.

This selection uses the existing Q3D v3 and HFSS family schema
identifiers; it chooses the SGB route the model is built on (`thin_film`
Route A, `solid` Route C). A Q3D/HFSS request payload without `modeling`, or
one written for the native builder, was written by an earlier SCGSim and is
refused; read it with the SCGSim commit that wrote it. The execution path never
infers or supplies a missing mode. Fresh requests declare layers
with `PhysicalLayerDeclaration` records in the single authored `LayerStack`
coordinate system; the
[physical representation contract](specs/physical-representation.qmd) lists
their fields. A film declaration carries its original normal thickness in
`physical_dimensions["normal_thickness_um"]`, and film physical-thickness
output reports that value without recomputing it from endpoints. The earlier
`PhysicalLayerSpec(physical_layer_id, kind, z_min_um, z_max_um, contact_side,
source_thickness_um=None)` record is removed, with the AEDT request's own
physical layers: the plan declares them with `PhysicalLayerDeclaration`. The physical layer ID is
counted once across polygons, occurrences, and Net membership; no per-layer
`stack_id` is introduced. Coordinate mapping uses endpoint spans; finite
volumes keep their own body extent.

The mode selection chooses geometry representation; it does not choose a solver
family or a public A/B/C execution route. The complete transform and material,
terminal, build-only, and failure behavior is defined in the
[AEDT Solid and thin-film contract](specs/aedt-runtime.qmd#aedt-solid-thin-film).
Q2D and Palace are outside this migration. Q3D input-v1/v2 request schemas
remain removed; shared V1/V2 handoff compatibility for other supported family
paths does not restore those Q3D request schemas or bypass the explicit-mode
requirement.

This extension introduced AEDT runtime-source identity
`scgsim.aedt.runtime-source.v15`. The current producer computes its list from
the AEDT import closure under v30, and a result recorded under an earlier
identity is read with the SCGSim commit that wrote it.

The AEDT Solid and thin-film contract linked above owns the occurrence-local
Ground and field-side/thickness distinctions for these modeling paths.

## Geometry API {#geometry-api}

The baseline `scgsim.sgb` facade maps to two surfaces. `scgsim.geometry` owns
source-facing planning, snapshots, normalized input records, the GDS and
stack-file adapter, vacuum preparation and detached summaries. The modules of
`scgsim.geometry.models` hold the canonical input and record definitions; each
name is imported from its defining module. A layout enters through
`GeometryPlan` and the simulation classes; `build_sgb_geometry` in
`scgsim.geometry.sgb` builds the model from a prepared input and sits below that
entry, so a direct call with an input built by hand assumes what the entry
guarantees (see [the supported entry](supported-scope.qmd#supported-entry)).
Each name below has one current definition, without an old-path compatibility
wrapper.


- **Baseline `scgsim.sgb` → current owner `scgsim.geometry`.** Declared names: `BoundaryCurveChainSpec`, `Coordinate`, `CurveKindLiteral`, `CurveOrientationLiteral`, `GdsBoundaryReconstructionSpec`, `GeometryBuildInput`, `GeometryPlan`, `GeometryPlanSnapshot`, `InputSummary`, `LayoutPolygonSpec`, `PathInput`, `PolygonRing`, `PortSheetOverlapRecord`, `PortSheetRegionRecord`, `RouteLiteral`, `SemanticEntitySpec`, `SourceCurveSpec`, `VacuumRegionSpec`, `Vector3D`, `apply_vacuum_region_to_stack`, `build_gds_stack_geometry_input`, `summarize_geometry_input`.
- **Baseline `scgsim.sgb.geometry_plan` → current owner `scgsim.geometry`.** Declared names: `GeometryPlan`, `GeometryPlanSnapshot`.
- **Baseline `scgsim.sgb.models` → current defining modules under `scgsim.geometry.models` (listed below).** Declared names: `BoundaryCurveChainSpec`, `ConductorPartRoleLiteral`, `ConductorRepresentationLiteral`, `Coordinate`, `CurveKindLiteral`, `CurveOrientationLiteral`, `DEFAULT_INTERFACE_SOLVER_USE`, `GdsBoundaryReconstructionSpec`, `GeometryBuildInput`, `HIGH_COUNT_LOCAL_CONDUCTOR_PART_ROLES`, `InterfaceKindLiteral`, `LayoutPolygonSpec`, `PathInput`, `PolygonRing`, `PortSheetOverlapRecord`, `PortSheetRegionRecord`, `RouteLiteral`, `SemanticEntitySpec`, `SolverUseLiteral`, `SourceCurveSpec`, `VacuumRegionSpec`, `Vector3D`.
- **Baseline `scgsim.sgb.vacuum` → current owner `scgsim.geometry`.** Declared names: `apply_vacuum_region_to_stack`.
- **Baseline route builder, `scgsim.sgb`, `scgsim.sgb.pipeline`, `scgsim.sgb.planning`, `scgsim.sgb.export` and `scgsim.sgb.validation` → no supported import.** Declared names: `SemanticGeometryBuilder`, `build_route_construction_plan`, `export_physical_group_records`, the stage functions (`plan_conductor_contact_patches`, `plan_cut_host_operations`, `plan_mm_contact_records`, `plan_route_construction_bodies`, `plan_route_surfaces`, `plan_route_tags`, `plan_route_volumes`, `plan_surface_partitions`, `recognize_route_interfaces`), every `validate_*` validator, and the plan records `BackendEntityTagRecord`, `ConstructionPlanRecord`, `CurvePlanRecord`, `CurveRefRecord`, `CutHostOperationRecord`, `FinalPhysicalGroupRecord`, `InnerPecVoidShellRecord`, `PointPlanRecord`, `RouteABConstructionPlanRecord`, `RouteABVolumePlanRecord`, `StructuredFinalPhysicalGroupRecord`, `SurfaceLoopRecord`, `SurfaceRefRecord`, `TagPlanRecord`, `VolumePlanRecord`, with the literals `DimensionLiteral`, `GmshDimTag`, `ROUTE_ALLOWED_REPRESENTATIONS`, `RUN_METADATA_DIR`, `SEMANTIC_GEOMETRY_METADATA_DIR`, `SurfaceLoopRoleLiteral`, `SurfaceOrientationLiteral` and `TagSourceKindLiteral`. Build a layout through `GeometryPlan` and `EigenmodeSim` or `ElectrostaticSim` from `scgsim.palace`; build a prepared input of your own with `build_sgb_geometry`.
- **Baseline component adapter, `scgsim.sgb.stack` and `scgsim.sgb.source_curves` → no supported import.** Declared names: `build_gdsfactory_geometry_input`, `build_component_stack`, `bind_source_curves`. A component with a `component_semantics` schema 2 declaration enters through `GeometryPlan`, which builds the stack from the PDK layer stack and carries the authored curve bindings itself.


Every defining model keeps one canonical class/type definition in a record
module of `scgsim.geometry.models`. `scgsim.geometry` re-exports the input
records it lists; the other records are imported from their defining module.
Direct aliases below enumerate the baseline submodule
entries that have a current owner. Each entry records the preferred supported
facade; a definition may live in a lower-level module to preserve dependency
direction.


- **Baseline `scgsim.sgb.adapter` → current defining module `scgsim.geometry.source.adapter`.** Declared names: `build_gds_stack_geometry_input`. Preferred API: `scgsim.geometry`.
- **Baseline `scgsim.sgb.geometry_plan` → current defining module `scgsim.geometry.source.plan`.** Declared names: `GeometryPlan`, `GeometryPlanSnapshot`. Preferred API: `scgsim.geometry`.
- **Baseline `scgsim.sgb.models.common` → current defining module `scgsim.geometry.models.common`.** Declared names: `Coordinate`, `CurveKindLiteral`, `CurveOrientationLiteral`, `PathInput`, `PolygonRing`, `RouteLiteral`, `Vector3D`. Preferred API: `scgsim.geometry`.
- **Baseline `scgsim.sgb.models.common` → current defining module `scgsim.geometry.models.common`.** Declared names: `ConductorPartRoleLiteral`, `ConductorRepresentationLiteral`, `DEFAULT_INTERFACE_SOLVER_USE`, `HIGH_COUNT_LOCAL_CONDUCTOR_PART_ROLES`, `InterfaceKindLiteral`, `SolverUseLiteral`. Preferred API: `scgsim.geometry.models.common`.
- **Removed by issue #67 (the native AEDT builder's planning).** `scgsim.geometry.planning` with `scgsim.geometry.models.topology` (`InterfacePlanRecord`, `MMContactRecord`, `SurfacePlanRecord`) and the construction records `ConstructionBodyPlanRecord` and `SurfacePartitionRecord`: AEDT imports the SGB model, so nothing calls them. No supported import replaces them.
- **Baseline `scgsim.sgb.models.input` → current defining module `scgsim.geometry.models.input`.** Declared names: `BoundaryCurveChainSpec`, `GdsBoundaryReconstructionSpec`, `GeometryBuildInput`, `LayoutPolygonSpec`, `SemanticEntitySpec`, `SourceCurveSpec`, `VacuumRegionSpec`. Preferred API: `scgsim.geometry`.
- **Baseline `scgsim.sgb.models.regions` → current defining module `scgsim.geometry.models.regions`.** Declared names: `PortSheetOverlapRecord`, `PortSheetRegionRecord`. Preferred API: `scgsim.geometry`.
- **Baseline `scgsim.sgb.summary` → current defining module `scgsim.geometry.source.summary`.** Declared names: `InputSummary`, `summarize_geometry_input`. Preferred API: `scgsim.geometry`.
- **Baseline `scgsim.sgb.vacuum` → current defining module `scgsim.geometry.source.vacuum`.** Declared names: `apply_vacuum_region_to_stack`. Preferred API: `scgsim.geometry`.


Shared polygon, spatial and Entity primitives sit below the source stage;
source code does not import planning. Source identity, snapshot detachment,
caller-owned final Net membership and native correspondence remain owned by
their current responsibilities.

The shared implementation modules use responsibility names. The grid
engine lives in `scgsim.geometry.grid`, including `grid_cache` and
`tagged_grid`; `source._normalization` and `source._occurrence` move to
`source.normalization` and `source.occurrence`, and `source._polygon_ops` to
`scgsim.geometry.grid.polygon_ops`. These
internal names do not expand the supported API; use the `geometry` facade
above.

Planning and tagged-grid modules follow the same responsibility boundaries.
Their supported routes remain the package facades:

| Implementation area | Use this supported import |
|---|---|
| Source assembly and occurrence preparation | `GeometryPlan` from `scgsim.geometry` |
| Physical representation preparation | `interpret_physical_geometry` from `scgsim.geometry` |
| Rectangular junction declaration and derivation | Use `RectangularJunctionSpec` and `with_rectangular_junctions` from `scgsim.geometry`, then call `interpret_physical_geometry` |
| Model construction for a Palace study | `EigenmodeSim` or `ElectrostaticSim` from `scgsim.palace`; `build_sgb_geometry` from `scgsim.geometry.sgb` for a prepared input of your own |

The responsibility modules are `scgsim.geometry.source.plan_assembly`,
`scgsim.geometry.junctions`,
`scgsim.geometry.grid.tagged_grid_faces`, and
`scgsim.geometry.grid.tagged_grid_operations`. They organize the
implementation without adding new supported imports.

The junction implementation derives exact partitions for explicitly declared
rectangular junctions. Source and AEDT preparation share the internal
`junction_contact_inventory(build_input, request)` service and
`JunctionContactRequest` record to resolve the source support and incident
conductors. These bridge names are not exports of `scgsim.geometry`; callers
declare requests through the geometry facade and use the standard
physical-interpretation step.

The new responsibility tree follows the existing boundaries:

- `aedt.specs` owns common, HFSS, Q2D and Q3D-v3 request records plus explicit
  family parsing. Q3D input-v1/v2 is not restored.
- `aedt.preparation` owns the SGB model for AEDT, the portable handoff that
  carries it and canonical cohort membership.
- `aedt.runtime.transaction` is the sole Desktop owner and receipt-state
  coordinator. Family runtimes own their native prepare/solve/export/readback;
  the narrow shared native helper owns neither a family nor Desktop.
- `aedt.epr` owns EPR models, source geometry, fields/cache and workflow.
  `aedt.results` owns strict handoff/result resolution, provenance,
  convergence, matrices and sealed EPR readers. Results do not start a solve.
- `aedt.presentation` owns display-only projections and plotting, with lazy
  imports kept out of strict result resolution.

`EigenmodeSim` stays the high-level mutable state owner for geometry/stack,
EPR settings, preparation and handoff invalidation. Preparation helpers do not
take over that state. Transaction ordering remains explicit: validate the
request and input cohort, write the running receipt before PyAEDT/Desktop,
perform one family transaction, persist returned facts before Desktop release,
then seal any saved EPR result. A prior native/family error remains primary if
release also fails; resolution validates returned artifacts without executing
AEDT. No shared Simulation base or common physical-result model is introduced.

The documented direct module surfaces migrate as follows: `spec` to
`specs.common/hfss/q2d/q3d/parse`; `handoff` splits among
`preparation.handoff`, `preparation.geometry` and `epr.workflow`;
`eigenmode` remains the state-owning facade; `resolve` moves to
`results.resolve`; and `run.main` remains at `scgsim.aedt.run` as a thin
delegate. The importable but non-exported `aedt.util` moves to an internal
I/O leaf and is not kept as a wrapper. EPR analysis, result readers, and
presentation modules move to their named owners above and in the responsibility
tree without expanding the package facade.

Keep `python -m scgsim.aedt.run`, its `main(argv)` and `__main__` behavior.
Generated handoff and EPR scripts continue to call that command with their
existing arguments. Transaction implementation moves behind the CLI shim.
Dynamic EPR workflow imports call the one transaction owner; EPR's HFSS
export/readback dependency becomes an explicit internal service. Visualization
imports current PyAEDT constants from the canonical spec owner without making
them public exports.

The current producer records runtime-source v30, computed on each use as the
import closure of every AEDT module and both AEDT visualization loaders; see
the [runtime-source contract](specs/aedt-runtime.qmd#runtime-source). Per-module
hashes bind the listed files, and the canonical manifest digest identifies that
source snapshot; neither is a permanent code value. Results recorded under an
earlier runtime-source schema are read with the SCGSim commit that wrote them;
old module strings are not mapped onto new paths. Handoff and receipt histories remain separate from Q3D request
versioning; Q3D remains v3 only. This map does not claim native Q3D completion.

## Palace meshing and Surface EPR {#palace-mesh-migration}

Palace now builds its geometry with SGB and meshes it with `scgsim.meshing`.
This section maps each removed mesh option to its replacement and lists the other
changes a Palace study has to make. The old options are removed with no
compatibility layer, so a script that passes one fails until it is updated.

### Geometry

`mesh()` builds the model with `build_sgb_geometry` from `scgsim.geometry.sgb`.
The baseline route builder has no current equivalent; see the
[Geometry API](#geometry-api).

### Mesh controls

`set_mesh` now takes `recipe`, `mesher`, `budgets` and `quality_threshold`; the
[Palace mesh controls](specs/palace-electrostatic-sgb.qmd#palace-mesh-controls)
define them. `set_mesh` changed alike on both facades, and
Eigenmode and Electrostatic share the defaults.

::: {.askr-table-compact}
| Removed | Replacement |
|---|---|
| `size_policy`, `refined_mesh_size`, `max_mesh_size`; `set_numerical(refined_mesh_size=, max_mesh_size=)` | `recipe`: `FeatureRecipe` (default), `GlobalSizeRecipe` or `UniformBoundaryRecipe` |
| `algorithm_3d` | `mesher=MesherOptions(algorithm_3d=...)`, with `scgsim.meshing.DELAUNAY` or `HXT` |
| `geometry_order`, `high_order_optimize` | `MesherOptions(geometry_order=..., high_order_optimize=...)` |
| `threads`, `surface_threads` | None. Meshing runs on one thread, because HXT with several threads was not reproducible. |
| none | `quality_threshold` (default 0.01 minSICN) and `budgets` (`Budgets`) |
:::

The recipe closest to each former sizing choice, and what changes when you switch,
is below. Neither recipe reproduces the old mesh element for element.

::: {.askr-table-compact}
| Former setting | Closest recipe | What changes |
|---|---|---|
| `scgsim_default` (refined 5 µm, maximum 300 µm) | `UniformBoundaryRecipe()` | Before, only the boundary curves of the `boundary_surfaces`, `pec_surfaces` and `port_surfaces` groups were sized, with settable sizes and 2D algorithm 5. Now every curve of the model is sized, the 2D algorithm comes from `MesherOptions` (pass `algorithm_2d=5` to match), and the threshold and repair apply. |
| `gmsh_default` (no size field) | `GlobalSizeRecipe()` | Before, Gmsh chose its own sizes with no maximum. Now the maximum size is the bounding-box diagonal over 20, `MesherOptions()` uses Delaunay (the benchmark that measured this recipe used HXT), and the threshold and repair apply. |
| `algorithm_3d`, `threads` | `MesherOptions(algorithm_3d=...)` | Meshing runs on one thread. |
:::

The default is none of these: `FeatureRecipe()` sizes the curves the geometry
calls for, with `MesherOptions()` (Delaunay) and `Budgets()`. A mesh that cannot
reach the quality threshold now raises `MeshRepairError` and stops the run,
where mesh quality never blocked a run before.

### Surface EPR

Surface-EPR margins became geometry, and the changes follow from that:

- Set Surface EPR on the plan, `plan.set_surface_epr(specs)` before
  `plan.prepare()` ([Surface EPR and the vacuum on the plan](#plan-owns-surface-epr)).
- The route and Surface EPR are two settings. `set_surface_epr(*, representation,
  specs, route_a_thin_film=None, approximation_profile=None)` became
  `sim.set_route(route, *, approximation_profile=None)` and
  `plan.set_surface_epr(specs)`. Route B is the default, so a Route B simulation calls
  neither for its route. Surface EPR is computed only when the plan was given
  specs, for Eigenmode and Electrostatic alike: drop the call that asked for
  none (Route B with empty `specs`), since an empty mapping is now refused, and
  use `plan.set_surface_epr(None)` to turn Surface EPR off again. Route A
  is `set_route("A")`, which lowers the films with the `thin_film` profile;
  `substrate_face` and `metal_gap_equivalent` are passed as
  `set_route("A", approximation_profile=profile)`. The keywords `representation`
  and `route_a_thin_film` are gone, and there is no `thin_film` keyword: the
  profile's name already says the lowering. The simulation's `thin_film` field and
  the `thin_film` key of `input_summary()` are gone with it; `input_summary()`
  shows the name of the profile the preparation uses, the default included.
- `inset_margins_um` asks SGB for bands. It accepts only positive, strictly
  increasing margins, so drop a leading `0.0`: the baseline row is always present.
- Palace no longer writes native `Mask` or `Inset`, so margin rows need no Palace
  fork build. The result readers reject a config that contains native `Mask` rows.
- `inset_margins_by_entity_um` is new, for per-conductor margins on `MA` and `MS`.
  `face_kinds` accepts `sheet`, `top`, `bottom` and `interface`, and rejects
  `sidewall` when the spec asks for margins.

The [Eigenmode contract](specs/palace-eigenmode.qmd#surface-epr-margins) defines
the keys and rows. SGB group names attach the face kind with `__`, as in
`MA::pad__top::band=1`; the rule is in the
[SGB design pages](../zh-TW/docs/design/sgb/identity.html#band-group-names).

### Results

Palace now writes mesh manifest `schema_version` 2 and index map `schema_version`
3, and reads only those. Run folders of older schemas and detached EPR results of
`scgsim.palace.epr-result.v1` are rejected, as described in
[Palace run schemas](report-model.qmd#palace-run-schemas). The renames below have no
old-name aliases.

::: {.askr-table-compact}
| Before | Now |
|---|---|
| `SurfaceMaskEprRecord`, `SurfaceMaskEprSeriesSnapshot` | `SurfaceMarginEprRecord`, `SurfaceMarginEprSeriesSnapshot` |
| `PhysicsQuantitiesReport.masked_snapshots` | `PhysicsQuantitiesReport.margin_snapshots` |
| `scgsim.palace.epr-result.v1` | `scgsim.palace.epr-result.v2` |
| `surface-mask-Q.csv` and `surface-mask-energy.csv` | Margin rows are read from `surface-Q.csv` |
:::

### Convergence and reports {#palace-convergence-migration}

`3.0.0rc2` adds the convergence declaration and changes what the reports show.

**Run folders written by `3.0.0rc1` or earlier are not read.** The returned
receipt is now version 2 and states how the solver ended. Result reading refuses
a version 1 receipt and names the commit that wrote it as the way to read that
folder; to read a study with this release, prepare and run it again.

New, and optional:

- `sim.set_convergence(...)` declares when a run has converged, with criteria
  on the capacitance, the mode frequencies, Surface EPR and Palace's error
  indicator ([declaration](specs/palace-electrostatic-sgb.qmd#convergence-declaration)).
  A change is a percentage of the value:
  `Capacitance.diagonal().within(percent=0.5)`. Palace is
  [stopped](specs/palace-electrostatic-sgb.qmd#convergence-stop) after the pass
  at which the criteria have converged, so the passes after it are not run. With
  a declaration `amr_tolerance` is set aside, and stating one is refused.
- `ResolvedPalaceResult.convergence` holds the check of every pass and the
  verdict, and `ResolvedPalaceResult.solver_end` how Palace ended.

Changed for every run, declared or not:

::: {.askr-table-compact}
| Before | Now |
|---|---|
| Run Identity showed every recorded field | Problem, Route, Profile, AMR passes recorded and MPI × OpenMP; the rest with `show_details=True` |
| `|Δ …| vs AMR pass` figures | Removed. With a declaration each quantity is followed by its declared change in percent |
| One surface figure with MA, MS and SA | One figure per interface kind, a line for the whole surfaces and one per inset |
| `show_physics_quantities()` opened with the surface ranking | It opens with the capacitance matrix, or each mode's frequency and Q |
| `show_all_results()`: trust, benchmark, physics | Trust, physics, benchmark |
| `show_simulation_benchmark()` took no `theme` | Every view takes `theme="light"` or `"dark"` |
| A capacitance figure named `C[1][1]` | Named by its terminals, `C[signal][signal]` |
:::

The layout of each view is in the
[report model](report-model.qmd#declared-convergence).

### Layout modeling check {#simulation-drc-migration}

`3.0.0rc3` changes the first argument of `simulation_drc` on
`scgsim.palace.EigenmodeSim`, `scgsim.palace.ElectrostaticSim` and
`scgsim.aedt.EigenmodeSim`: it is the `GeometryPlan` the simulation will be
given, before `prepare()`. `layer_stack`, `material_records`, `instances` and
`nets` are gone; they are the plan's. `route`, `approximation_profile` and
`modeling` stay; the Surface-EPR specs are the plan's too
([below](#plan-owns-surface-epr)). A first argument that is not a
`GeometryPlan` is refused with the plan to build.

```python
# Before
EigenmodeSim.simulation_drc(component, layer_stack=layer_stack, material_records=material_records, nets=nets, route="A")

# Now
plan = GeometryPlan(component=component, root_id="chip", layer_stack=layer_stack, material_records=material_records, coupon_padding_um=0.0)
plan.set_nets(nets)
plan.set_vacuum_region((0.0, 0.0, 1000.0))  # when the layer stack has no VACUUM_REGION
plan.set_rectangular_junctions([...])  # when the layout has rectangular junctions
EigenmodeSim.simulation_drc(plan, route="A")
```

The check adds nothing to the plan. Before, it checked with zero coupon
padding and, when the layout had no vacuum, a vacuum padded by (0, 0, 1000) µm;
now it uses the plan's coupon padding and vacuum, and a plan without a vacuum
is refused with the simulation's own error. Register an assembly's instances
with `plan.register_instance` before `set_nets`. The AEDT check now covers the
plan's rectangular junctions, their sheets cut. `prepare_hfss_driven_from_geometry`
and `prepare_q3d_from_geometry` now run the import's first step before they
write the handoff, so they refuse a model the import cannot realize. See
[Layout modeling check](layout-modeling-check.qmd#build-the-plan).

### Surface EPR and the vacuum on the plan {#plan-owns-surface-epr}

From `3.0.0rc4` the Surface-EPR specs and the vacuum region are set on the
`GeometryPlan`, once, and nowhere else (issue #268): both change the geometry
and neither depends on the solver. The simulation reads them from the snapshot
`set_plan` binds, and `simulation_drc` from the plan it is given. The removed
calls have no compatibility layer.

::: {.askr-table-compact}
| Removed | Replacement |
|---|---|
| `sim.set_surface_epr(specs)` on `scgsim.palace.EigenmodeSim`, `scgsim.palace.ElectrostaticSim` and `scgsim.aedt.EigenmodeSim` | `plan.set_surface_epr(specs)` before `plan.prepare()`; `None` turns it off and `{}` is refused, as before |
| `sim.set_vacuum_region(padding)` on the Palace simulations | `plan.set_vacuum_region(padding)` before `plan.prepare()` |
| `simulation_drc(plan, surface_epr_specs=specs, ...)` on all three classes | `plan.set_surface_epr(specs)`, then `simulation_drc(plan, ...)`; `route`, `approximation_profile` and `modeling` stay |
| The `surface_epr_specs` and `vacuum_region` constructor arguments of the Palace simulations, and `surface_epr_specs` of `scgsim.aedt.EigenmodeSim` | The plan's setters; `sim.surface_epr_specs` reads the bound plan's specs |
| `scgsim.aedt.EigenmodeSim.set_geometry(...)`, `set_stack(...)` and its `component`, `build_input` and `stack` arguments | `sim.set_plan(plan.prepare())`, the only source |
:::

```python
# Before
sim = EigenmodeSim()
sim.set_plan(plan.prepare())
sim.set_vacuum_region((0.0, 0.0, 1000.0))
sim.set_surface_epr(specs)
EigenmodeSim.simulation_drc(plan, surface_epr_specs=specs, route="A")

# Now
plan.set_vacuum_region((0.0, 0.0, 1000.0))
plan.set_surface_epr(specs)
EigenmodeSim.simulation_drc(plan, route="A")
sim = EigenmodeSim()
sim.set_route("A")
sim.set_plan(plan.prepare())
```

The specs are checked by the same rules, against the plan's materials, when
they are set and again by `prepare()`. The simulations that compute Surface
EPR read them: Palace Eigenmode and Electrostatic and HFSS Eigenmode. HFSS
Driven Terminal and Q3D do not read them and cut no bands, as before. A
refusal that named `set_surface_epr` on the simulation now names
`GeometryPlan.set_surface_epr`. The model, the Palace configuration and the
run folders are unchanged: a run folder written by `3.0.0rc3` is read as
before.

## Palace package symbols

`scgsim.palace` declares 26 package-facade names. The inventory groups them by
their v2 responsibility owner.


- **Current owner and responsibility:** `scgsim.palace.simulation`; the two simulation classes on one shared core and lifecycle. **Facade exports:** `ElectrostaticSim`, `EigenmodeSim`.
- **Current owner and responsibility:** `scgsim.palace.simulation.drc`; the two-stage `simulation_drc` report and its refusal, also raised by `mesh()` before meshing. **Facade exports:** `SimulationDrcError`, `SimulationDrcReport`, `StageResult`.
- **Current owner and responsibility:** `scgsim.palace.results.resolved_records`; the checked records of a returned run. **Facade exports:** `PalaceCost`, `PalacePerformance`, `PalaceProvenance`, `PalaceReturnedReceipt`, `ParsedTable`.
- **Current owner and responsibility:** `scgsim.palace.reports.resolved_result`; the resolved result a user holds, with its notebook views. **Facade exports:** `ResolvedPalaceResult`, `resolve_palace_result`.
- **Current owner and responsibility:** `scgsim.palace.results.epr` and `scgsim.palace.results.epr_records`; detached EPR values and offline reanalysis. **Facade exports:** `PalaceEprResult`, `epr_result`, `reanalyze_epr`, `resolve_epr_result`.
- **Current owner and responsibility:** `scgsim.palace.reports`; solver-specific plot over detached EPR. **Facade exports:** `show_epr`.
- **Current owner and responsibility:** `scgsim.palace.results.inspection_records`; detached data records consumed by Palace reports. **Facade exports:** `PalaceFailureDiagnosis`, `PalaceResultSelection`, `PassCostRecord`, `SurfaceMarginEprRecord`, `SurfaceMarginEprSeriesSnapshot`.
- **Current owner and responsibility:** `scgsim.palace.reports`; trust, physics and benchmark views over retained result evidence (`reports.reports`, `reports.trust`, `reports.views`). **Facade exports:** `PalaceTrustReport`, `PhysicsQuantitiesReport`, `SimulationBenchmarkReport`, `inspect_run_trustworthiness`.


## Palace direct submodule exports

These non-underscored modules declare their own `__all__` and therefore need
explicit migration entries in addition to the package facade.


- **Baseline direct import `scgsim.palace.electrostatic` → current owner `scgsim.palace.simulation.electrostatic`.** Declared symbols: `ElectrostaticSim`.
- **Baseline direct import `scgsim.palace.eigenmode` → current owner `scgsim.palace.simulation.eigenmode`.** Declared symbols: `EigenmodeSim`.
- **Baseline direct import `scgsim.palace.handoff` → current owner `scgsim.palace.run.handoff`.** Declared symbols: `HandoffPlan`, `HandoffProfile`, `prepare_handoff`.
- **Baseline direct import `scgsim.palace.resolve`.** Declared symbols: `PalaceCost`, `PalacePerformance`, `PalaceProvenance`, `PalaceReturnedReceipt`, `ParsedTable`, `ResolvedPalaceResult`, `resolve_palace_result`. Current owners: the records in `scgsim.palace.results.resolved_records`, `ResolvedPalaceResult` and `resolve_palace_result` in `scgsim.palace.reports.resolved_result`; import them from `scgsim.palace`.
- **Baseline direct import `scgsim.palace.report`.** Declared symbols: `AmrPassSnapshot`, `PalaceFailureDiagnosis`, `PalaceResultSelection`, `PalaceTrustReport`, `PassCostRecord`, `PhysicsQuantitiesReport`, `inspect_run_trustworthiness`. Current owners: `inspect_run_trustworthiness` in `scgsim.palace.reports.reports`, `PalaceTrustReport` in `scgsim.palace.reports.trust`, `PhysicsQuantitiesReport` in `scgsim.palace.reports.views`, and the data records in `scgsim.palace.results.inspection_records`; import them from `scgsim.palace`.


The current `scgsim.palace.results.inspection_records` module defines
`AmrPassSnapshot`, `PalaceFailureDiagnosis`, `PalaceResultSelection`,
`PassCostRecord`, `SurfaceEprRecord`, `SurfaceEprSeriesSnapshot`,
`SurfaceMarginEprRecord`, and `SurfaceMarginEprSeriesSnapshot`. Each module
declares only what it defines; the package facade `scgsim.palace` is the
import path for every supported name.

`scgsim.palace._epr_results` is a baseline private implementation path whose
supported names are re-exported by `scgsim.palace`. Its current owner is
`scgsim.palace.results`; the old private import path is not a compatibility
surface.

## Visualization symbols


- **`GeometryPreview`, `GeometryPreviewArtifact` → `scgsim.visualization.preview`.** Responsibility: Source-bound preview object and returned artifact/unavailable mode.
- **`inspect_palace_geometry` → `scgsim.visualization.loaders.palace`.** Responsibility: Read the Palace mesh, manifest, index map and config into semantic preview modes.
- **`inspect_aedt_geometry` → `scgsim.visualization.loaders.aedt`.**
  Responsibility: Bind AEDT native/receipt identity and load solver-assigned
  geometry. A raw `.aedt` path requires explicit `aedt_version` and design; a
  sealed run folder uses its bound spec version without an override.
- **Scene records and shared rendering → `scgsim.visualization.scene`, `scgsim.visualization.rendering`.** Responsibility: Keep scene construction and rendering reusable without taking solver physics or simulation status ownership.
- **Shared loader file-identity helpers → `scgsim.visualization.loaders.common`.** Responsibility: One loader-level implementation for JSON, hash and confined-path observations.


The `scgsim.visualization` package facade continues to export exactly
`GeometryPreview`, `GeometryPreviewArtifact`, `inspect_aedt_geometry`, and
`inspect_palace_geometry`. Preview files and their manifest remain separate
from solver and handoff identity. Palace previews retain high-order cell
connectivity and node coordinates; source curves and native curved-arrangement
facts remain in the mesh manifest and detached mesh summary. These facts are
not discarded during relocation.

## Shared presentation

The baseline `scgsim._notebook_presentation` module contains physics-neutral
formatting helpers used by geometry and AEDT. Its current implementation is
`scgsim.presentation.notebook`. The formatting helpers do not own Palace or
AEDT projections, calculations, or result status; their presentation remains
solver-specific. Moving this private helper does not make its function names a
new public API.
